summary: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson (1840–1890) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1858–1861). He later served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

Edwin Gerow (1931–2018) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1985–1997) and was Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1985–1997).

Edwin Norris (1795–1872) worked in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology, and taught John Dowson. He held posts as a junior clerk at the East India Company (1818–1837), translator at the Foreign Office (1847–1866), and secretary and librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society.

Edwin Whitfield Fay (1865–1920) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins, and Leipzig University. He held positions at the University of Michigan, Washington and Lee University, and the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda (1926–2010) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen Women's College, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Eido Tai Shimano (1932–2018) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa, and attended the University of Hawaiʻi. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and held posts at New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

Eiichi Imoto (1930–2014) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1953). He held academic posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1996) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1996–2001).

Eiichi Makino (1878–1970) worked in philosophy and other fields. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903), he taught there (~1903–1938) and held posts at Kyushu, Tohoku, and Chuo Universities, as well as Shiraume Gakuen Junior College.
Eiichi Yamaguchi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and later served as a Research Assistant there (attested 1991).
Eiki Hoshino (1943–) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He later served there as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director (~1980–2013).

Eisaku Okada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). His career includes appointments with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2014), Koyasan University (attested 2014), and Kyoto University (attested 2015).
Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1976) and as president of Doho University (attested 1976).

Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1933–1937) and under Gyoo Kageyama. He held posts at Rissho University (~1949–1984) and Minobusan University.
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
Eiyin Yasuda (1938–) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gyōin Hashimoto around 1950 and completed studies at Ryukoku University.
Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sōkatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen Kyodan.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College. He held posts as Rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji, Professor at Toyo University, and researcher at Toyo Bunko.

Eki Nakayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2020) and held a research fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2020).

Ekyo Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Göttingen. He held academic posts at Nagaoka University of Technology and the University of Tokyo.
Ekyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).
